findings.issue: P123-R11 is not closed: present-tense layer numerals spelled as words survive. Both docstrings say 'this module (layer two)' about _status_facts, which _deps.LAYERS holds at index 3, so these are the same off-by-one class P123.33/P123.54/P123.65 were opened for. layer_mention_drift() returns [] only because _LAYER_WORD_NUMERAL is r'\blayers?[\s-]+\d+' and reads digits alone, while CLAUDE.md states that a number in prose may be spelled as a word and _output._numeral_span() already reads both spellings. P123.65's task text asks the lint to refuse ANY layer numeral and to delete every existing one. No lmd case plants a word-spelled numeral, so lmd1 is green over a tree that still carries a wrong one.
findings.resolution: Read the numeral through the shared word-or-digit reader (_output._numeral_span or its table) in _LAYER_WORD_NUMERAL, delete the two 'layer two' mentions (keep the reasoning), and add an lmd3 shape ('this module (layer two)') plus a prove-gates RED row for the word spelling. While there, decide on the ordinal 'BOTTOM LAYER' claims (_priority.py:28, _ado_parent.py:33, _ado_tracked.py:53, _manifest_io.py:674): all four modules sit at LAYERS index 2, not the bottom.

findings.issue: P123-R14 is not closed. Its resolution had two halves: restore the lines, and find what rewrote them before it touches non-test code. P123.69 restored the three named lines. The same artefact (an existing 'X = Y' rewritten to 'X =Y') is still in the phase diff three more times, and one of them is in product code: audit-lookup.py:766 'lines =[...' findings.issue: Outcome agreement is the right invariant for R10, because guard-bash-writes runs PostToolUse only and the pre-command disk cannot be reread. _config.copy_destinations' docstring now says what holds. The new comment in _statement_targets, though, says taking both landings 'costs nothing ... never makes a finding of its own'. That is false under the deny tier: a path in `named` goes to `authored` and is BLOCKED even while a peer session is active (`clauses`), and the union adds a directory destination the shared reader alone did not give. For `cp -r src/ lib/` with lib pre-existing, the is_dir=False reading adds `lib`, and writing_statement's directory rule (:776-779) then names every changed path under lib/. A peer's concurrent write to lib/other.py is attributed to this command and blocked instead of noticed. The (ca) cases compute `named` only over files the copy landed, so they cannot see over-attribution.
findings.resolution: Either restrict the extra is_dir=False landing to destinations that did not exist as directories before (or to the specific <dest>/<source-basename> subtree), or correct the comment to state the deny-tier cost. Add a (ca) negative: a file under the destination directory that the copy did not write is not named.

findings.issue: The fail-closed branches of verdict_returns are unpinned: verdict_commit naming no commit, a merged side whose returns git will not list, and rev-list failing. The executor states this ('the could-not-establish path is unpinned'). A regression that turned any of them fail-open would land an unseen diverges return with no case going red. The cannot-see list in landed_answers_refusal's docstring also no longer names any post-verdict history change. A rebase of the phase branch onto the target after the verdict rewrites the verdict commit so that it holds the target's later return, and that return then reads as seen.
findings.resolution: Add a vr24c case that makes the verdict commit unnameable (e.g. a tip whose plan-dir history holds no verdict-recording run) and asserts the refusal names why. Add the rebase-after-verdict shape to the cannot-see sentence.
